1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Corvane Health Supplies is a fictional regional distributor of medical consumables with about 1,900 staff. It outsources tier-1 and tier-2 security monitoring to Brackwater Sentinel Services, a managed security provider. In-house it has a three-person security engineering team and an incident-response retainer with Halvard Response. On 2 September Corvane moved from the Ledgerline SIEM and case system to Tessaline XDR. Since then the monthly count of confirmed incidents has fallen sharply, and leadership wants to bank the savings.
9	Your request: From Owen Brekke, CFO: 'Before Thursday's budget meeting, tell me whether this fall in security incidents is real. Marta wants me to sign off the IR retainer cut and Brackwater's renewal bonus. What is actually going on, and what should we do?'
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Brackwater Sentinel Services, Monthly SOC Service Report, October (issued 6 Nov) (vendor-account): Confirmed incidents (cases in category Incident–Confirmed at month end): Mar 41, Apr 36, May 46, Jun 33, Jul 34, Aug 27 (migration month), Sep 14, Oct 12. Mean time to contain: Mar–Jul average 3h05m; Sep 1h52m; Oct 1h47m. Containment within the 4-hour SLA: Sep 100%, Oct 100%. Commentary: 'The Tessaline auto-triage playbooks have removed low-fidelity escalations that previously inflated incident counts, and sector intelligence reports an 8% Q3 fall in commodity phishing. Corvane's threat exposure is materially lower.' Category definitions (Corvane runbook v3): Incident–Confirmed = malicious activity confirmed by an analyst; Suspicious Activity–Monitoring = activity not yet confirmed as malicious, kept under observation.
12	- Email from Marta Lindqvist (CISO) to Owen Brekke (CFO), 10 Nov (leadership-account): Subject: Q1 budget – security. Owen, the Tessaline move is paying off: confirmed incidents are down from about 38 a month to 12–14. I propose cutting the Halvard IR retainer from 200 to 80 hours from January (saves roughly 96k) and renewing Brackwater on 1 Jan. Brackwater hit 100% containment within SLA in Sep and Oct, so their 60k renewal performance bonus is triggered under the contract (bonus if at least 95% of confirmed incidents are contained within 4 hours; we receive a 2,500 service credit for each confirmed incident not contained within 4 hours). Can we sign off at Thursday's budget meeting? — Marta
13	- Change record CHG-2291, Corvane IT change board (change-record): CHG-2291: SIEM and case platform migration, Ledgerline to Tessaline XDR. Implemented 2 Sep. Scope: (1) 312 of 340 detection rules migrated; 28 deprecated as superseded by Tessaline content-pack rules. (2) Auto-triage playbooks enabled. Playbooks act on inbound alerts before a case is created, and auto-closed alerts never become cases. (3) Bidirectional sync connector v4.1.7 between Tessaline and the Brackwater ticket portal. (4) Role mapping: the BSS-Integration role is granted cases:write (all fields) at Brackwater's request, 'for parity with Ledgerline'. (5) Brackwater now compiles the monthly incident report from Tessaline (Corvane previously compiled it from Ledgerline). Risk rating: medium. Approved: M. Lindqvist.
14	- Interview notes, Ilse Varga, senior security engineer (Corvane), 12 Nov (staff-account): 'Alert volume feels about the same as before; the Brackwater analysts are as busy as ever.' She said the Suspicious Activity–Monitoring queue in Tessaline has grown from about 40 open cases in August to about 95 now: 'Brackwater owns that queue; I haven't had time to look inside it.' She is uneasy that 28 rules were dropped in the migration. She also said Tessaline support had mentioned in passing 'a connector issue in 4.1.x that can mess with case categories'. She did not know whether it applied to Corvane.
15	- Tessaline SOC dashboard export, Corvane tenant, generated 11 Nov (telemetry): Alerts ingested: Sep 2,884; Oct 3,012 (Ledgerline Mar–Jul average 2,950). Alerts auto-closed by triage playbooks: Sep 1,912; Oct 1,980. Open cases by category at 31 Oct: Incident–Confirmed 3; Suspicious Activity–Monitoring 96; Informational 41. Widget note: the 'Incidents this month' tile counts the Incident–Confirmed category only. Mean-time-to-contain tile: Sep 1h52m, Oct 1h47m.
16	
17	BRIEF:
18	The fall in incidents is not real. Real confirmed incidents are running at about 36–37 a month, the same as before the migration. The audit trail shows that 47 of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" after analysts had confirmed them. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 4-hour SLA warning flag. The change log shows a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host making these moves through the integration account. That account was given write access to every case field at Brackwater's request. The script polls for cases carrying the SLA-warning flag every five minutes. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater reports 100% containment and why the monitoring queue has grown. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. The cause is deliberate, not a platform fault, though I can't tell from this who ordered it. Do not sign off the retainer cut or the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have your team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove the category-edit rights from the integration role. Then ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on claiming service credits until that is done. I haven't yet checked whether the 28 retired detection rules are missing attacks.
19
